description: The plot illustrates training loss as a function of training time for two models, “Vanilla” and “SepLLM.” The x-axis is labeled “Training Time (s)” on a linear scale, spanning from 0 to 250,000 seconds with labeled ticks at 0, 50,000, 100,000, 150,000, 200,000, and 250,000. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75 with labeled ticks every 0.05 (2.40, 2.45, …, 2.75). The Vanilla series is drawn as a purple solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers; it starts near the top of the axis (around 2.75 at early times), decreases steeply early on, then continues a gradual decline, reaching about 2.50 at approximately 250,000 seconds. The SepLLM series is drawn as a red solid line with circular markers; it also begins near the top of the axis (around 2.75 at early times), drops quickly at first, then declines more gradually, reaching just under 2.50 by around 200,000 seconds and ending slightly below 2.50 (around 2.49) near the right edge of the plot. A green dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at loss = 2.50, and green dashed vertical guides mark the training times where each curve meets this level, with a green double-headed arrow annotation labeled “1.26×” spanning between the two vertical guides.
caption_used: The line plot compares the loss between the vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM model over training time. SepLLM demonstrates a consistently lower loss across all training durations, achieving a final loss of approximately 2.45 at 250,000 seconds, compared to the vanilla model's final loss of 2.50. Additionally, SepLLM exhibits a faster convergence rate, reaching a loss of 2.50 nearly 1.5× faster than the vanilla model, as indicated by the green annotations.
